I haven't checked whether everything is pushed or whether the branch can be deleted. From the repo's actual clone, run:

```
git fetch --prune
git status -sb                                   # uncommitted changes, ahead/behind on current branch
git log origin/<branch>..<branch> --oneline      # local commits not pushed (empty = pushed)
git branch -r --merged origin/main | grep <branch>   # merged into main by ancestry
git cherry -v origin/main <branch>               # "+" lines = commits whose changes aren't in main
```

The branch is safe to delete if:
- `git log origin/<branch>..<branch>` prints nothing,
- the branch shows up in `--merged`, or `git cherry` shows no `+` lines (squash or rebase merges fail the `--merged` check but pass `cherry`),
- `git status` is clean.

If all three hold, run `git branch -d <branch>` and `git push origin --delete <branch>`. Use `-d`, not `-D`, so git refuses to delete the branch if it isn't merged.
